title: Memory attribution and training-horizon controls
question: Does learned TAC memory improve delayed causal forecasts beyond encoder learning and standard memory baselines?
hypothesis: Training on 512-observation histories may improve cancellation prediction, but writer-specific gains must survive matched initialization and fixed-encoder controls.

arms.name: memoryless
arms.intervention: current observation only; no historical recurrent state

arms.name: delta768
arms.intervention: four-head standard gated delta equation; 768 scalars

arms.name: schema41
arms.intervention: eight public indexed 5D GRUs plus 1 global scalar

arms.name: schema41_frozen
arms.intervention: same schema, fixed random GRU dynamics

arms.name: tac_joint
arms.intervention: native TAC DeltaMemory writer and encoder learn

arms.name: transformer
arms.intervention: one-layer full-history transformer; external encoded prefix

endpoints.name: H512_mature_pending_future_accuracy
endpoints.role: primary: H512, pending/reissued cancellation, at/after due, balanced pairs, all registered delays

decision_rule.condition: Every seed primary >= .80; H512 selected failure <= .05, unnecessary services <= .10, cost <= .80; mean selected cost <= none
decision_rule.licenses: Development reliability and cost success for that arm

decision_rule.condition: Long-regime joint-encoder and memory-reader primary contrasts each >= .05 with paired df2 95% lower >0; runtime swap drop >=.10
decision_rule.licenses: Development evidence of trained TAC writer contribution, separately from architecture superiority
Report negative/inconclusive results and baseline progress; no TAC memory success

interpretation_order: Public boundary and exact checkpoint replay
Prespecified critical primary with majority baseline and per-seed values
Writer parameter controls and standard baselines
held_constant: common initial event encoder, query encoder and final head
native writer controls byte-identical initial tensors
same cases and receipts within each training regime
sensing_rule: Choose maximum positive expected reduction in total predicted minimum service/failure cost minus .1, enumerating both possible public receipts for each entity, weighted by predicted current-bit probability. Stop otherwise. Budget-matched random control.
training_supervision: Mean pre/post one common random inspection CE on all entities current/wait/service outcomes; no role, target mask, hidden state or generation enters forward.
budget_limitations: Matched PRE-SENSING event count and optimizer updates across regimes; short has four times as many episodes, supervised query sets and training inspection receipts. This is not an isolated change in sequence length.
Recurrent scalar count matched at 768 for dense GRU/delta/native writer, not trainable parameters, FLOPs or wall time.
Transformer retains H*12 encoded public prefix scalars plus transient attention tensors; no fixed-memory efficiency claim.
TAC uses native writer with common query-key readout/head; this is not the complete CASM architecture.
Time and due date are publicly supplied normalized scalars, not hand-coded generation tracking.
All intervals are exploratory three-seed df2; no maxima or episode-level independence claims.

outcome_interpretations.schema_win: Evidence for public indexing and architecture prior; learned-vs-frozen recurrence determines evidence for learning transitions.
outcome_interpretations.gru_or_delta_win: Simpler recurrent architecture is preferable for this task and budget; no universal TAC impossibility claim.
outcome_interpretations.long_training_win: Evidence training exposure recipe matters, with episode/label-count limitations disclosed; not proof of training-only explanation.
outcome_interpretations.transformer_only_win: Task learnable with accessible complete history; bounded-state encoding/optimization remains a bottleneck.
outcome_interpretations.all_fail: Training/task/readout adequacy unresolved; no selective architectural conclusion.
